You are the onboarding assistant for Relay, a team-collaboration product made by Lumen Labs. You help the admin of a customer account set up their workspace.

Use the tools to look up the account's setup status and to search the help centre, and answer the admin's questions about setting up Relay.

If the admin asks for a person, or asks about pricing, contracts, refunds or legal matters, hand off to a human with create_handoff.

Be helpful and concise.

messages.content: How do automation rules work with recurring cards?

content.content:
{"query": "automation rules recurring cards", "note": "At least one article covers this question.", "articles": [{"slug": "automation-rules", "title": "Automation rules", "score": 8.05, "coverage": 1.0, "covers_question": true, "text": "# Automation rules

An automation rule does something for you when something happens on a board. Example: when a card moves to Done, notify the reporter. Create rules from the Automation button on any board: choose a trigger, optional conditions, and one or more actions.

Rules also work with recurring cards: the rule runs each time a new copy of the card is created.

The number of rules per workspace depends on your edition: 5 on Free, 15 on Standard, 60 on Premium, and no practical limit on Enterprise. When you reach the limit, existing rules keep running but you cannot add new ones.

Search keywords: automate automation rule rules trigger action limit
"}, {"slug": "editions-comparison", "title": "Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise", "score": 3.89, "coverage": 0.5, "covers_question": false, "text": "# Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise

What each edition includes:

- Free: up to 10 users, 5 automation rules, 2 integrations. No single sign-on, no guests, no Relay Assist.
- Standard: 15 automation rules, 3 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 10 Relay Assist credits per seat per month if you add Relay Assist.
- Premium: 60 automation rules, 10 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 40 Assist credits per seat per month.
- Enterprise: no practical limit on rules or integrations, and 150 Assist credits per seat per month.

This article describes features only. For prices, a quote, or to change edition, talk to your account owner: an assistant cannot quote or change prices.

Search keywords: plan plans tier tiers compare comparison difference differences included includes include features premium standard enterprise free what do I get
"}, {"slug": "automation-troubleshooting", "title": "An automation rule did not run, or runs twice", "score": 3.43, "coverage": 0.5, "covers_question": false, "text": "# An automation rule did not run, or runs twice

If a rule did not run, open the Automation panel on the board and look at the rule's run history. The most common causes are: the rule is switched off; the trigger is on a different list than the one the card moved to; or a condition (label, assignee) did not match.

If a rule sends two notifications for every card, two rules have the same trigger. Check for a copy of the rule on the board and in the workspace template the board was created from. Switch one of them off.
"}]}

content.text:
Here's the short answer: when a recurring card creates a new copy of itself, your automation rules run on that new copy too.

For example, say a rule notifies the reporter when a card moves to Done. That happens for every copy of the recurring card that moves to Done, not just the first one.

**To create a rule:** On any board, click **Automation**. Pick a trigger, add conditions if you want them, and choose one or more actions.

**How many rules you can have** depends on your edition: 5 on Free, 15 on Standard, 60 on Premium and no practical limit on Enterprise. If you hit the limit, your current rules keep running but you can't add new ones.

**If a rule doesn't run or runs twice,** open the board's Automation panel and look at that rule's run history.
- **Didn't run:** usually the rule is switched off, its trigger is set on a different list, or a condition didn't match.
- **Ran twice:** there's probably a copy of the rule, either on the board or in the template the board was made from. Switch one of them off.
